name: AWeirdDev/flights
what_it_holds: Python package ('fast-flights') scraping live Google Flights results (prices, routes, airlines, stops, duration, emissions) via base64-encoded protobuf against Google's internal flight-search endpoint, no API key. MIT licensed, 2,047 stars, v3.0, actively updated (commits as of 14 Sep 2026). No committed price data itself -- a live acquisition method a human would need to run and archive over time to build a fare panel.
why_useful: Airfare levels are a travel-demand/consumer-discretionary proxy that reads on ABNB nights and ADR (kernel analogue per gap list). Fastest available method to start a point-in-time airfare pull; would need daily cron to become a vintage series (gap 4).
themes: Airline fare tracking datasets (Google Flights scrapers, Skyscanner, Hopper reports), airfare price indices
why_all: Airfare levels are a travel-demand/consumer-discretionary proxy that reads on ABNB nights and ADR (kernel analogue per gap list). Fastest available method to start a point-in-time airfare pull; would need daily cron to become a vintage series (gap 4).

Could be run point-in-time (with sign-off, since it touches a non-Airbnb site) to build a forward-looking domestic/international airfare panel as a travel-demand and consumer-strength proxy (gap 6/10) or FX-adjusted travel-cost input; also the best-maintained reference implementation if the team ever needs a Google Flights client.

name: i-baumann/DB1B_Automation
what_it_holds: Automates downloading/cleaning BTS DB1B + T100 to replicate a transportation-economics paper: produces multimarket contact indices, hub variables, HHI market-concentration measures, outsourcing proportions, network-size metrics. No longer maintained (archived note: "as of 2025 I am no longer maintaining this"). MIT licensed. No data committed.
why_useful: Lowers the cost of building a US domestic airfare/traffic panel from the official DOT source named in gap 10.
themes: Airline fare tracking datasets (Google Flights scrapers, Skyscanner, Hopper reports), airfare price indices
why_all: Lowers the cost of building a US domestic airfare/traffic panel from the official DOT source named in gap 10.

An academic-replication-style pipeline over DB1B/T100 producing airline market-structure metrics (HHI, hub concentration) that could serve as a competitor-capacity/consolidation cross-check (gap 10), though unmaintained and possibly stale against current BTS file formats.

name: Trevorkaaya21/airline-market-power-analysis-
what_it_holds: Python/pandas analysis of US domestic DB1B fares: HHI, price dispersion, demand elasticity by market. Unverified whether raw DB1B extract or only derived tables are committed; described as pandas-based market-power study.
why_useful: Could be a source of ready-processed route-level fare/elasticity output rather than raw DB1B, saving reprocessing time if it holds committed CSVs.
themes: Airline fare tracking datasets (Google Flights scrapers, Skyscanner, Hopper reports), airfare price indices
why_all: Could be a source of ready-processed route-level fare/elasticity output rather than raw DB1B, saving reprocessing time if it holds committed CSVs.

Another DB1B-based analysis that might have derived, smaller CSVs (price dispersion / elasticity by route) more directly usable than the raw multi-GB BTS files; worth a closer look if the team pursues a US-fare-elasticity angle.

name: nyc-subway-turnstile-data
what_it_holds: Ruby/PostgreSQL pipeline that downloads MTA turnstile files directly from the MTA site from 2014-10-11 onward and loads them into a `turnstile_observations` table; committed `lib/stations.csv` maps station/line/division to borough; weekly automated refresh (Saturdays) driving a public dashboard. 121 stars, MIT, actively maintained (updated Apr 2026).
why_useful: Gives station- and borough-level NYC subway entries/exits back to 2014 as a leading/coincident visitor-flow proxy for the NYC market (ABNB's largest single US city); could be aggregated to a monthly NYC subway volume series to compare against Inside Airbnb NYC nights.
size_hint: raw MTA weekly turnstile files, not committed; only a small station-mapping CSV committed
themes: Public transit ridership and airport rail links (MTA, TfL, RATP, JR) as visitor proxies; ridership open data
why_all: Gives station- and borough-level NYC subway entries/exits back to 2014 as a leading/coincident visitor-flow proxy for the NYC market (ABNB's largest single US city); could be aggregated to a monthly NYC subway volume series to compare against Inside Airbnb NYC nights.

name: mta-data
what_it_holds: Pulls the MTA's 2023 Subway Origin-Destination Ridership Estimate (~116M rows, scaled-up OMNY/MetroCard tap-and-swipe data) from NYC Open Data (Socrata) via `data-exporter.py` into a 2.5GB DuckDB file; aggregated by month/day-of-week/hour for every station pair with station lat/long; includes PDF data dictionary and a Jupyter analysis notebook.
why_useful: Origin-destination granularity could isolate airport-linked lines (JFK AirTrain/LIRR, LaGuardia, Newark) or tourist-corridor station pairs as a finer NYC visitor-flow proxy than raw entries/exits.
themes: Public transit ridership and airport rail links (MTA, TfL, RATP, JR) as visitor proxies; ridership open data
why_all: Origin-destination granularity could isolate airport-linked lines (JFK AirTrain/LIRR, LaGuardia, Newark) or tourist-corridor station pairs as a finer NYC visitor-flow proxy than raw entries/exits.
